safety_lead_time.comparison_action: increase SAP safety lead time from 3.5 to 5.1 days

narrative: Material PL1__M6DD6978 displays intermittent/lumpy demand with a CV of 1.79 and only 31% active demand days, punctuated by a statistically significant upward trend. Lead times average 2.62 working days with moderate variability (CV=0.40). The (r,Q) policy with SS=238 and OQ=629 was selected because EOQ-based ordering nearly halves replenishment frequency versus MOQ-only ordering while the safety stock closes the zero-buffer gap in the current SAP configuration to achieve 95% service level. The combined peak inventory of 867 units is well within the 3,502-unit storage limit.
warnings: DEMAND PATTERN: Intermittent/lumpy demand (CV=1.79, non-zero fraction=31.3%) — normal-approximation SS is conservative; robust SS of 188 units is a lower bound
TREND: Statistically significant upward demand trend detected (p<0.00001) — refresh demand parameters regularly
SAP SAFETY STOCK: Current ERP safety stock is 0 units — no stockout buffer in production system
COST: Optimized policy increases total annual cost by $186.48 to achieve 95% service level target

research_insights.selection_rationale: The (r,Q) policy is appropriate for a high-CV intermittent material with a meaningful annual volume (~11,665 units). It triggers replenishment at a fixed reorder point covering mean lead-time demand plus safety stock, and orders a fixed EOQ-derived quantity that minimises total ordering and holding cost. The MOQ of 303 is comfortably below the EOQ of 629, so the EOQ governs and no MOQ distortion arises.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is not binding: peak inventory (SS+OQ=867) uses only 24.8% of the 3,502-unit limit. No capacity-driven order reduction was required.
